questions.exp: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit. It is the primary component of a computer that executes instructions of a program by performing basic arithmetic, logic, control and I/O operations.

questions.q: The binary number system uses which digits?
questions.exp: The binary number system uses only two digits: 0 and 1. All computer data is ultimately stored and processed as binary (base-2) numbers.

questions.q: Who is known as the Father of Computers?
questions.exp: Charles Babbage is known as the Father of Computers. He designed the first mechanical computer, the Difference Engine, in the early 19th century.
WWW stands for World Wide Web. It was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989. It is a system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the Internet.
RAM stands for Random Access Memory. It is the primary memory of a computer that stores data and instructions currently in use. It is volatile, meaning data is lost when power is off.

questions.q: The first computer virus was called?
questions.exp: The Creeper program (1971) is often cited as the first computer virus. It spread through ARPANET and displayed the message 'I'm the creeper, catch me if you can!'
HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol. It is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. HTTPS is the secure version with encryption.

questions.q: 1 GB is equal to how many MB?
questions.exp: 1 GB (Gigabyte) = 1024 MB (Megabytes). Similarly, 1 MB = 1024 KB, and 1 KB = 1024 bytes.

questions.q: The programming language Python was created by?
questions.exp: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its simplicity and readability.

questions.q: Which company developed the Android operating system?
questions.exp: Android was developed by Android Inc., which was acquired by Google in 2005. Google then released Android as an open-source operating system in 2008.
